cards.name: Your development workspace
cards.description: Use the client you already work in.

cards.name: Run it your way
cards.description: A team server, your own client, or a workflow.

setups.title: Local MCP configuration
setups.note: Node.js 22+ runs the published npm package on your computer. Replace the URL and PAT locally; keep credentials out of Git.

setups.title: Add from your terminal
setups.note: Commands shown for macOS, Linux and WSL. Install the selected client and Node.js 22+. Replace the URL and PAT before running; the command stores them in your local client configuration.

setups.title: Connect to your team server
setups.note: Use your own deployed HTTPS URL. There is no public Polarion relay. Your server must be reachable by the client provider; an administrator sets up TLS, OAuth and exact redirect allowlists.

setups.title: VS Code MCP configuration
setups.note: Node.js 22+ is required. VS Code uses a servers object. Select the tools you need in chat; the full catalog can exceed the client tool budget.

setups.title: Zed context server
setups.note: Node.js 22+ is required. Zed uses context_servers, with command, args and env directly inside the server entry.

setups.title: Claude Messages API
setups.note: Add these fields to your Messages request. Enable the mcp-client-2025-11-20 beta header. The Polarion PAT authenticates to this server; your Anthropic API key authenticates the API request.

setups.title: OpenAI Responses API
setups.note: Add this tools field to a Responses request. Use your OpenAI API key for the API request and your Polarion PAT for the MCP server.

setups.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
setups.note: Use inside your async application with openai-agents installed and Agent imported from agents. Run the agent while the server context is open. Keep API keys and PATs in your application secret store.

setups.title: Custom GPT Actions
setups.note: This uses the REST wrapper and its HTTP_API_KEY, not the MCP endpoint or the user PAT. The reduced schema contains 30 actions. A team administrator deploys the REST wrapper first.

setups.title: Docker team server
setups.note: The image starts Streamable HTTP. Each client sends its own Polarion PAT as Authorization: Bearer <PAT>. Local endpoint: http://localhost:3000/mcp. Add TLS and OAuth before connecting cloud clients.

setups.title: Any stdio MCP client
setups.note: Node.js 22+ is required. The client owns stdin and stdout. Configure this as its subprocess; it is not a standalone web service.

setups.title: REST wrapper / OpenAPI
setups.snippet:
docker run -d --name polarion-rest \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  -e API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 \
  -e BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT \
  -e HTTP_API_KEY=YOUR_WRAPPER_API_KEY \
  -e PUBLIC_URL=https://YOUR-SERVER \
  ghcr.io/phillipboesger/polarion-mcp:1.4.0 \
  node build/http-server.js
setups.note: All calls use the deployment PAT. Clients send Authorization: Bearer <HTTP_API_KEY>. Serve this behind HTTPS; schemas are at /openapi.json and /openapi-gpt.json.

setups.title: n8n HTTP Request
setups.note: This setup uses the REST wrapper. Its administrator configures API_BASE_URL, BEARER_TOKEN and HTTP_API_KEY. Store the wrapper key in an n8n credential after importing.

clients.name: Claude Desktop
clients.label: Desktop
steps: Open Claude Desktop Settings > Developer > Edit Config.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save, fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Claude web / Desktop connector
clients.label: Web connector
steps: Get your team’s HTTPS MCP URL. The administrator enables OAuth and the Claude redirect preset.
Open Customize > Connectors > Add custom connector. Paste the URL below. Choose Register automatically for this server’s DCR flow.
Connect, enter your Polarion PAT on the server login page, and enable the connector in a conversation.
clients.note: On Team / Enterprise, an owner adds the connector under Organization settings > Connectors > Add > Custom > Web; members then choose Connect.

clients.name: Claude Code
clients.label: Code
steps: Install Claude Code and Node.js 22+.
Replace the URL and PAT, then run the command below.
Start Claude Code, open /mcp, and confirm Polarion is connected. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”
clients.snippet: claude mcp add --env API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 --env BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT --transport stdio polarion -- npx -y polarion-mcp

clients.name: Claude API
clients.label: API
steps: Deploy or obtain a reachable HTTPS MCP server.
Add the snippet to your Messages request and set the beta header named below. Replace URL and PAT.
Send a request with your model, max_tokens and messages. Check the returned tool results.

clients.name: ChatGPT connector
clients.label: ChatGPT
steps: Get your team’s HTTPS MCP URL. The administrator enables OAuth and allowlists the exact callback shown by ChatGPT.
In ChatGPT Plugins, choose + > Add custom MCP server. Paste the URL and select OAuth with dynamic client registration (DCR).
Install the resulting plugin, sign in with your Polarion PAT, and select it with @ in a conversation.
clients.note: Custom MCP access depends on your ChatGPT workspace permissions. Use DCR for this server unless the administrator explicitly enabled CIMD.

clients.name: Custom GPT Actions
clients.label: Custom GPT
steps: Get your team’s deployed REST wrapper URL and HTTP_API_KEY.
In the GPT editor, open Actions > Create new action > Import from URL and paste the schema URL below.
Choose API Key authentication, Bearer type, and enter HTTP_API_KEY. Test getProjects in the editor.

clients.name: OpenAI Responses API
clients.label: API
steps: Get a reachable HTTPS MCP server and your Polarion PAT.
Add the snippet to your Responses request, replacing URL and PAT.
Send a request with your model and input. Review and approve MCP tool calls.

clients.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
clients.label: Agents SDK
steps: Install openai-agents and import Agent from agents in your async app.
Paste the snippet inside an async function. Replace URL and PAT.
Run the agent with Runner while the MCP server context is open.

clients.name: Codex
clients.label: Codex
steps: Install Codex and Node.js 22+.
Replace the URL and PAT, then run the command below.
Open Codex and inspect /mcp. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”
clients.snippet: codex mcp add polarion --env API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 --env BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT -- npx -y polarion-mcp

clients.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
clients.label: Copilot Studio
steps: Open your agent’s Tools page, then Add a tool > New tool > Model Context Protocol.
Enter a name, description and the URL below. Choose API key > Header, named Authorization.
Create a connection with the value Bearer YOUR_POLARION_PAT. Add the tool and test the agent.
clients.note: Use generative orchestration. This path uses a PAT header and does not require an OAuth callback. Select only the tools your agent needs.

clients.name: VS Code / GitHub Copilot
clients.label: VS Code Copilot
steps: Run MCP: Open User Configuration from the Command Palette.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save, start the server and trust it when prompted. In agent chat, select Polarion tools. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Gemini CLI
clients.label: Gemini CLI
steps: Install Gemini CLI and Node.js 22+.
Replace the URL and PAT, then run the command below.
Start Gemini CLI and inspect /mcp. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”
clients.note: Run Gemini in a trusted folder. If the server shows Disconnected, use gemini trust to trust that folder.
clients.snippet: gemini mcp add --scope user --env API_BASE_URL=https://YOUR-POLARION/polarion/rest/v1 --env BEARER_TOKEN=YOUR_POLARION_PAT polarion npx -y polarion-mcp

clients.name: Cursor
clients.label: Cursor
steps: Open your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json, or create it. Do not put a PAT in a shared project file.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save and reconnect the server. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Windsurf / Cascade
clients.label: Windsurf
steps: In legacy Cascade, open the Actions (...) menu > MCPs > Open MCP config file.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save and reconnect the server. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”
clients.note: The vendor now documents this as legacy Cascade in Devin Desktop. Its 100-tool budget requires selecting a subset of Polarion tools. This config does not apply to the Devin Local agent.

clients.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
clients.label: JetBrains
steps: Open Settings > Tools > AI Assistant > Model Context Protocol (MCP), add a server and choose STDIO.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Click OK and Apply. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Zed
clients.label: Zed
steps: Run zed: open settings file from the Command Palette.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save and reconnect the server. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Cline
clients.label: Cline
steps: Open Cline > MCP Servers > Configure > Configure MCP Servers.
Paste the snippet, merge with existing settings, and replace the Polarion URL and PAT.
Save and reconnect the server. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Docker team server
clients.label: Docker
steps: Install Docker and replace the Polarion REST URL in the command.
Run the container. Connect a local HTTP client to http://localhost:3000/mcp with Authorization: Bearer YOUR_POLARION_PAT.
For a team, put a TLS proxy in front, set allowed hosts to its hostname, and configure OAuth for cloud connectors.

clients.name: Generic stdio client
clients.label: stdio
steps: Open your client’s local MCP server settings.
Set command to npx, arguments to -y polarion-mcp, and pass API_BASE_URL and BEARER_TOKEN as environment variables, as shown below.
Let the client launch the process, then list its tools. Ask: “List the Polarion projects I can access.”

clients.name: Generic HTTP client
clients.label: HTTP
steps: Obtain your team’s MCP server URL, or start the Docker server for local use.
Paste your HTTPS URL below into the Streamable HTTP setting, or use http://localhost:3000/mcp for local Docker. Add Authorization: Bearer YOUR_POLARION_PAT.
Connect and list tools. For OAuth-capable clients, use your administrator’s login configuration instead.

clients.name: REST wrapper / OpenAPI
clients.label: REST / OpenAPI
steps: Install Docker. Replace the Polarion URL, deployment PAT, wrapper key and public HTTPS URL in the command.
Run the container and route HTTPS traffic to its loopback port.
Import /openapi.json into your integration, or /openapi-gpt.json into Custom GPT Actions. Send HTTP_API_KEY as a Bearer token.

clients.name: n8n REST workflow
clients.label: n8n
steps: Get a deployed REST wrapper URL and its HTTP_API_KEY from your administrator.
Add an HTTP Request node, choose Import cURL and paste the command below after replacing the server URL.
Replace the imported Authorization header with a Bearer Auth credential containing HTTP_API_KEY, then execute the node. The shell variable in the snippet is a placeholder.
clients.note: Use the HTTP Request node as a workflow step or attach it as a tool to an AI Agent.
clients.referenceNote: This confirmed path uses REST. The MCP Client Tool documentation still describes an SSE Endpoint, so it is not used as evidence for a Streamable HTTP setup here.
